information.text: Design, engineering, and product thinking converge in my daily practice—building expressive, structured experiences.
paragraphs: I’m Julián Galindo, a Design student at Universidad de los Andes, focused on video games, interfaces, and digital experiences. I’m graduating in 2028, and I enjoy anything that involves creating, exploring, and understanding how people interact with what they use.

I like observing, questioning, and analyzing why something works the way it does. I enjoy thinking in systems, how things connect, and how good design can make an experience clearer, more pleasant, and more human. I’m a mix of the technical and the sensitive: I like structure, but also aesthetics; logic, but also emotion.

Films, video games, and music shape how I see design: as a way to tell something, to build atmospheres, and to create moments that feel genuine. I’m constantly interested in learning, refining my visual judgment, and finding new ways to turn ideas into experiences that truly make sense.

inspirations.text: I draw inspiration from interactive media, architectural composition, and minimalist interface systems.

portfolio.title: Digital
portfolio.quote: Showcasing creativity and technical excellence through a unified digital presence.

description.paragraph1: This portfolio website serves as a comprehensive digital showcase of my professional work, technical skills, and design expertise. Built with modern web technologies, it provides visitors with an intuitive and engaging way to explore my projects, view my certifications, and understand my capabilities as both a developer and designer.
description.paragraph2: The project emphasizes clean design, smooth interactions, and accessibility across all devices, demonstrating my commitment to creating user-centered digital experiences that balance aesthetics with functionality.

portfolio.context: Nowadays, potential employers and clients expect to see working examples of a candidate's skills. Then, the creation of a digital portfolio becomes essential to effectively demonstrate one's abilities.
portfolio.problem: Usually, designers and developers create very different portfolios for showcasing their work, making it hard to find a balance between design and development skills. Many portfolios focus solely on visual appeal or technical prowess, neglecting the importance of integrating both aspects in a unified way. This project aims to solve that problem by creating a unified platform that highlights my dual expertise in design and development.

phases.title: Research & Discovery
phases.description: I began by analyzing 30+ developer and designer portfolios, identifying common patterns, standout features, and areas where most portfolios fell short. This research phase helped me understand what makes a portfolio memorable and effective.
bullets: Analyzed successful portfolio structures and navigation patterns
Created user personas representing recruiters, hiring managers, and clients
Defined core features: project showcases, skills display, certifications
Established design principles: clarity, accessibility, personality

phases.title: Information Architecture
phases.description: Mapped out the site structure, organizing content into logical categories that would make sense to different types of visitors based on their goals and interests.
bullets: Created site map with clear hierarchies and relationships
Designed navigation system with categorized project types
Planned content flow from hero to projects to contact
Structured data for easy internationalization

phases.title: Design & Prototyping
phases.description: Created wireframes and high-fidelity prototypes in Figma, iterating on layouts, color schemes, and interaction patterns. Focused on creating a design system that would be consistent, scalable, and maintainable.
bullets: Designed modular component system with reusable patterns
Established color palette supporting both dark and light themes
Created responsive layouts for mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints
Prototyped key interactions and animation sequences

phases.title: Development
phases.description: Built the site using React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, prioritizing clean code, component reusability, and optimal performance from the start.
bullets: Implemented component-based architecture with React 19
Integrated i18next for full bilingual support
Incorporated interactive Spline 3D models for engaging visual experiences
Created custom animations using Tailwind and CSS
Optimized images and assets for fast loading times
Implemented lazy loading for improved performance

phases.title: Testing & Refinement
phases.description: Conducted comprehensive testing across devices, browsers, and network conditions. Gathered feedback from peers, mentors, and potential users to refine the experience.
bullets: Tested on iOS, Android, Windows, and macOS devices
Verified accessibility with screen readers and keyboard navigation
Optimized performance using Lighthouse and Chrome DevTools
Implemented fixes based on real user feedback
Conducted A/B testing on key interactions

candelaria.title: Candelaria
candelaria.quote: Design, build, and deploy the complete digital presence of a high-performance university competition team.

myRole.title: My Role
myRole.description: Product Engineer, UX/UI Designer, Full-stack Developer

description.paragraph1: Candelaria is the complete digital presence of a university engineering competition team. The site goes beyond a static portfolio: it integrates member management, publications, memberships, donations, a merchandise store, and a gamification system for followers, all under a kinetic, high-contrast visual identity.
description.paragraph2: The project was born from the need to centralize team communication, facilitate external support, and offer a user experience that matches the technical level of the team. From database architecture to color palette, every decision was made with product and engineering judgment.

problem.intro: University competition teams usually end up with partial solutions: an Instagram account, a PDF with their achievements, and a generic donation link. Candelaria needed something different:
bullets: A platform that reflects the team's technical and visual identity.
A system that allows external supporters to contribute financially with real traceability.
An internal panel where leaders can manage members, publications, and roles without touching code.
Support for two payment markets: international (Stripe) and Colombia (PayU).
A long-term incentive to keep followers engaged: gamification.

phases.title: Research & Design System
phases.description: Definition of the 'Neon Velocity' visual system in Figma, covering typography, color palette, components, and grids. Designed 6 final screens (Home, Vehicle, Team, Publications, Support, About) with a mobile-first approach and cinematic vertical scrolling.
bullets: Defined 'Neon Velocity' design system in Figma
Designed 6 final screens with a mobile-first, cinematic scrolling approach
Built design system with Tailwind CSS 4 and Class Variance Authority (CVA)
Established component variants and layout rhythm for all main views

phases.title: Architecture & Backend
phases.description: Designed the data model in PostgreSQL with Django 4.2 and Django REST Framework: 13+ models covering teams, members, publications, payments, and tiers. Dual authentication system with djangorestframework-simplejwt for internal and external users.
bullets: Designed 13+ model schema in PostgreSQL with Django 4.2 and DRF
Dual auth system: internal team users and external supporters via JWT
Secure whitelist for leadership role assignment with manual approval and audit logging
Supabase integration for profile sync, media storage, and PL/pgSQL gamification

phases.title: Frontend & Integrations
phases.description: Single-page application in React 19 with React Router DOM 7 and Vite 7. Full internationalization (Spanish/English) with i18next. Shopping cart and checkout flow with Stripe and PayU, including HMAC-SHA256 verified webhook handlers.
bullets: SPA in React 19 with React Router DOM 7 and Vite 7
Full Spanish/English internationalization with i18next
Shopping cart and checkout with Stripe (international) and PayU (Colombia)
HMAC-SHA256 webhook verification and real-time supporter tier calculation

phases.title: Performance & Deployment
phases.description: Query optimization using Django ORM's select_related(), prefetch_related(), and .only(). Image compression with vite-plugin-imagemin and media served via Supabase Storage. Monolithic deployment on Vercel with frontend on / and Django backend on /api/*.
bullets: Query optimization with select_related(), prefetch_related(), and .only()
Image compression with vite-plugin-imagemin
Media served via Supabase Storage
Monolithic deployment on Vercel: frontend on /, backend on /api/*

visualDesign.description: A kinetic, high-contrast, editorial aesthetic inspired by motorsport telemetry and high-precision technical design.

patterns.name: Forms

auth.title: Authentication & User Management
auth.description: Dual profile system: internal users (team members) with whitelist and leadership roles, and external users (supporters and buyers). Complete registration, login, password recovery, and profile management flow.

ecommerce.title: E-Commerce & Payments
ecommerce.description: Merchandise store (hoodie, cap, bottle), memberships at 3 levels ($5 / $10 / $25 USD), and free donations in COP/USD. Persistent cart, checkout with Stripe (international) and PayU (Colombia), purchase history per user.

gamification.title: Gamification: Supporter Tiers
gamification.description: Score is calculated as: total donated (COP) + months of membership × 5,000 COP. Calculated in PL/pgSQL on Supabase and exposed via REST API.

dashboard.title: Internal Dashboard
dashboard.description: Exclusive panel for team members: member management, role assignment, article publishing with PDFs, leader whitelist administration, and transaction review.

multilingual.title: Multilingual Support
multilingual.description: Full Spanish/English support with i18next. All backend models store fields in both languages (_en / _es) and the API responds based on the language parameter.

security.title: Security
items: Rate limiting on auth endpoints (10 req/min) and brute-force protection (8 attempts / 15 min)
HMAC-SHA256 webhook verification with timestamp tolerance (5 min)
Idempotent payment processing to avoid double-counting
Audit logging of all administrative actions
Security middleware: CSRF, configured CORS, security headers

reflections.description: Candelaria was the project that forced me to think like a product engineer, not just a developer. Making architecture decisions — when to use Django vs Supabase, how to model the tier system, how to abstract two payment providers — required reasoning about real trade-offs, not just implementing features.
reflections.keyLearning: The biggest learning was designing for two audiences with completely different needs: an external supporter who wants to contribute with one click, and a team leader who needs to manage people and publish content. Building a single platform that serves both without either feeling the interface wasn't designed for them was the most interesting design challenge of the project.
